data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if the test's own installation is not part of the subject's failure surface. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss occurs because compile.py is both the subject and the installer: mutations to compile.py can disable the very mechanism that would report them. Ordinarily-guarded modules show 4/4 to 6/7 because their tests are installed by a separate authority, so a mutation in the module cannot reach back and silence the test. The asymmetry is a property of self-installing subjects, not of test quality.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If compile.py's lost mutation was in a pure function with no interaction with the guard registry, the reflexivity mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 modules also self-install but still catch all mutations, then self-installation alone is not the constraining condition.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an independent second harness could be written to catch the lost compile.py mutation without changing compile.py, then the constraint was a design choice, not a structural limit.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 distribution is explained by mutation difficulty rather than observer-subject coupling, the claim is confounded.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When the test and the subject share a code path, a mutation can corrupt both the behaviour under test and the test's ability to report failure. This is a reflexivity confound: the subject modifies its own observer. The 3-of-26 result counts mutations that land in the shared observer-subject boundary, where no independent signal exists. The distribution is explained by the degree of coupling between each module and the test harness that guards it.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
